newsitem.title: USA: Maine lawmaker urges speedy vote on clear-cutting.
newsitem.headline: Maine lawmaker urges speedy vote on clear-cutting.

text.p: Maine Representative William Lemke, D-Westbrook, urged the new legislature to set an early date for a special statewide referendum on clear-cutting, a forestry practice used by the paper industry.

A measure proposed by Gov. Angus King, which would limit the timber practice to 75 acres, must go before the voters again because it failed to capture at least 50 percent of the votes that were cast in the Nov 5 elections.
And a more radical measure, which would entirely have banned the practice, got less than one-third of the vote.
Under the state constitution, an up-or-down vote on the governor's alternative to the so-called Ban Clearcutting proposal cannot occur for at least 60 days.
Lemke said waiting for the next statewide election in one year could hurt the state economy.
Governor Angus King said he plans to ask the State Supreme Court for a ruling on when a special election may be held.
